description: Table 2 is a small two-row data table rendered as an image, with no graphical axes, error bars, scale bars or legends. The header row gives the stub "Steel" followed by four austenite-condition column labels, "4Al_γ", "6Al_γ", "8Al_γ" and "10Al_γ". The single data row is labelled "γ_SFE (23 °C)/mJ·m⁻²" and reports the room-temperature stacking-fault energy of austenite: 51.25 for 4Al_γ, 62.64 for 6Al_γ, 68.47 for 8Al_γ, and an en-dash "–" for 10Al_γ, i.e. no value is given for the 10 Al steel. The table therefore demonstrates that γ_SFE increases monotonically with Al content over 4 → 6 → 8 wt.% Al, from 51.25 to 68.47 mJ·m⁻² (about +17 mJ·m⁻²). The caption states this is "γ at room temperature"; the citing text states the γ_SFE was calculated using thermodynamic functions and parameters listed in literature [35] and that ρ is the molar surface density along {111} planes while ΔG^γ→ε is the molar Gibbs energy of the γ→ε transformation. The missing 10Al_γ entry is consistent with that steel being nearly fully ferritic in the paper's abstract. All cell contents are legible.

subfigures.description: A two-row table: header row 'Steel | 4Al_γ | 6Al_γ | 8Al_γ | 10Al_γ'; data row 'γ_SFE (23 °C)/mJ·m⁻² | 51.25 | 62.64 | 68.47 | –'. Reports the calculated room-temperature stacking-fault energy of austenite for the four Al contents, with no value given for 10Al_γ.

observations.observation: The table is captioned 'Table 2 γ at room temperature' and its single data row is headed 'γ_SFE (23 °C)/mJ·m⁻²', i.e. the stacking-fault energy of austenite measured/quoted at 23 °C.
Column labels as printed are 4Al_γ, 6Al_γ, 8Al_γ and 10Al_γ under the stub 'Steel'.
No γ_SFE value is reported for 10Al_γ; the cell contains only an en-dash '–'.
The table shows γ_SFE increasing monotonically with Al content across the 4, 6 and 8 Al steels (51.25 → 62.64 → 68.47 mJ·m⁻²).
The citing text states the γ_SFE values were calculated using thermodynamic functions and parameters listed in literature [35].

The citing text defines ρ as the molar surface density along {111} planes, ΔG^γ→ε as the molar Gibbs energy of the γ→ε phase transformation, and σ as the interfacial energy per unit area of the γ/ε phase boundary — the quantities entering the γ_SFE calculation tabulated here.

The paper abstract states the microstructure evolves from single austenite at 4%Al to a ferrite-based duplex steel at 8%Al and nearly fully ferrite at 10%Al, which is consistent with no austenite SFE being listed for 10Al_γ.
